summary: Backend-only testing of the temporary MongoDB reconciliation endpoints (iteration 6). Created /app/backend/tests/test_iteration6_migrate.py (17 pytest cases, 17/17 PASSED) against the public preview URL. Validated: GET /api/_diag/db (200, mongo_scheme=mongodb+srv, mongo_host=cluster0.fjomnjr.mongodb.net sanitised, db_name=albarka, 18 collection counts, no credential fragments in the body); GET /api/_admin/migrate-mongo/inventory RBAC (no token -> 403, garbage bearer -> 401/403, client1 -> 403, superviseur -> 200 with db_name/mongo_host/collections/users_preview and no password_hash or _id leaked); POST /api/_admin/migrate-mongo guards (no token -> 403, client -> 403, wrong confirm_token -> 400 'confirm_token incorrect', target==source -> 400 'La cible est identique a la source', missing fields -> 422, unreachable target URL -> 502); dry_run=true with target=Atlas/albarka_dryrun -> 200, backup_dir=null, inserted/updated/errors all 0 and target collection stayed empty (verified directly via pymongo); only_collections=['users'] -> report.collections has exactly one key 'users'; skip_collections=['users'] excludes it; real migration of report_templates into albarka_dryrun -> run1 inserted=1, run2 inserted=0/skipped=1 with no duplicate ids (idempotence verified in the target DB); backup=true real run creates backup_dir; admin protection -> after seeding albarka_dryrun.users with admin@sawalismartsystems.com holding a sentinel password_hash + is_active=false, migration returned protected_partial=1, the sentinel hash and is_active=false were preserved while non-protected fields (full_name) were synced, and a non-protected user's password_hash was fully overwritten as expected. Production DB 'albarka' untouched (users=5, report_templates=1 after tests). Also re-ran the full existing suite: 206 passed / 1 skipped after fixing 2 stale pre-existing tests (unrelated to migration).

minor.issue: Public (unauthenticated) information disclosure: exposes the Atlas hostname, the DB name and per-collection document counts. Acceptable only as a very short-lived diagnostic - must be removed or moved behind require_roles(['superviseur','direction']) before/at prod cut-over.

Backups are written unencrypted to /app/backend/backups/mongo-*/ and users.json contains password_hash for every user (3 pre-existing dumps found on disk). The path is not git-ignored. Recommend writing outside the repo (/tmp or object storage), redacting password_hash, and adding cleanup.

Runs synchronously in the request; a full migration is reported at 60-90s while the ingress proxy times out at 30s. Needs a background task + status endpoint (or chunked only_collections runs) for the real cut-over.
source_db[name].find({}).to_list(100_000) silently truncates any collection above 100k docs and loads whole collections into memory - use a cursor / bulk_write batches.

confirm_token is hardcoded in albarka_migrate.py ( _CONFIRM_TOKEN ) instead of coming from an env var; target_mongo_url is taken from the request body (arbitrary outbound connection, staff-only but still SSRF-shaped).
Ephemeral collections are migrated by default (otps=481 docs, cron_runs=100) - add them to a default skip list, otherwise stale OTP/cron state is copied to the target.

No index creation on the target DB: the unique indexes (users.email, client_reports.number, cron_runs.run_id, notification_log.key) are only created on the connected source at startup, so the migrated target starts without dedup protection until the app is repointed and restarted.
Pre-existing robustness bug (unrelated to migration): raises KeyError when the passed user dict lacks 'id' (user['id'] used for notifiable_contacts_for) - use user.get('id').

action_items: Before/at prod cut-over: protect or delete GET /api/_diag/db (currently public) and remove the whole /_admin/migrate-mongo router as planned.
Make the real migration resilient to the 30s ingress timeout (background job + status endpoint) or document the chunked only_collections procedure.
Do not keep password-hash backups inside /app/backend/backups; redact or relocate and git-ignore.
Add default skip_collections for otps/cron_runs and create target indexes after migration.
Fix user.get('id') in albarka_notifications.notify_echeance (pre-existing KeyError risk).
Optional review: notify_echeance no longer returns a 'skipped' flag and still notifies tenant contacts when the main user account is inactive/opted-out - confirm this is the intended business rule.
critical_code_review_comments: albarka_migrate.py: in the protected-email branch update_one is called without upsert=True yet stats['inserted'] is incremented when matched_count==0 - dead/misleading branch (the 'existing' guard makes it unreachable).

albarka_migrate.py: non-'users' collections without an 'id' field fall back to find_one(doc) exact-match dedup, which is O(n) and treats any modified document as new (duplicate risk on re-runs) - settings uses _id and would be re-inserted with a new _id.
albarka_migrate.py: no per-collection timeout/limit and no partial-progress report if the request is cut off mid-run; the caller cannot know what was already migrated.

success_rate.backend: 100% (17/17 migration cases; full suite 206 passed / 1 skipped)

seed_data_creation: Target DB 'albarka_dryrun' on the same Atlas cluster now contains migrated report_templates (1), settings (1) and users (5, with a sentinel password_hash + is_active=false on admin@sawalismartsystems.com used for the protection assertion). contact_groups was dropped there. Production DB 'albarka' was never written to. One backup dir /app/backend/backups/mongo-*Z (settings.json only) created by the backup test.

If the router is removed after the prod cut-over, delete that test file. Two stale tests were repaired this iteration (missing 'id' in user dicts + removed 'skipped' key in notify_echeance's return).
rca_of_the_issue: No functional defect found in the migration feature itself; all requested scenarios behave as specified. The two regression failures seen initially were stale test expectations: notify_echeance now dereferences user['id'] (KeyError on id-less dicts) and no longer returns a 'skipped' flag; test fixtures/assertions were updated accordingly (test-side only, no product code changed).
